_comment: Target packet skeleton for evm-token-due-diligence. scripts/rpc_probe.py writes the machine-filled fields (tool, generated_at_utc, requested (chain_name and source stay null for you), observed, identity, cache, pin, pinned_block_hex, runtime, metadata (accounting_model stays null for you), probes, coverage_status, limitations, calls, failed_calls, declarations, notes). You fill deployment, candidate_pools, related_contracts, decision_question, requirement_frame, scope_statement, known_limitations, requested.chain_name/source, metadata.accounting_model, and _freeze. The target is always the TOKEN; a vault/pool/locker named by the user is resolved to its token first and enters related_contracts with its own role. Packet-to-manifest mapping (references/target-packet.md): drop keys starting with '_' and the schema-disallowed keys identity, cache, pinned_block_hex, probes, calls, failed_calls, coverage_status, observed.client_version_note, runtime.is_contract, runtime.runtime_status, runtime.proxy.implementation_code_size, metadata.*.selector, metadata.*.raw, metadata.*.qualifier, declarations.read_only_methods_only, notes, tool, packet_version; move requested.address_checksum -> target.address_checksum, runtime.runtime_status -> scope_addresses[0].runtime_status, pin -> pins[] (primary_pin_id P1), limitations -> coverage.limitations, related_contracts -> scope_addresses (after the target entry), raw metadata/probe return data -> evidence rows cited via metadata.*.evidence_id; add manifest_version "1.0", mode, declarations.simulation, declarations.external_content_untrusted, verdict (with conditional), report, and the target itself as scope_addresses[0] (role token, provenance user_supplied, runtime_status contract, code_hash = runtime.code_hash, material true). Chain ids and every other chain-specific number are as observed from the endpoint and must be verified at use time (eth_chainId at the pin).
_comment_generated_at_utc: UTC time the probe ran, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.

requested._comment: Exactly what the user asked for. chain_id (integer) is authoritative and is REQUIRED in this skill (--chain-id): a chain NAME from the user is mapped to the commonly cited id in references/chains/chain-verification.md section 6 and the mapping is recorded in source (e.g. "user said 'Base'; mapped to commonly cited id 8453, confirmed by eth_chainId"). chain_name is a label only. address is as supplied (strict: mixed case must satisfy EIP-55); address_checksum is the EIP-55 form used everywhere else (manifest: target.address_checksum). source = where the address came from (message, file, link) plus any chain-name mapping. The probe leaves chain_name and source null; you fill them.

observed._comment: What the endpoint reported. chain_id = int(eth_chainId), read live, never from cache. rpc_endpoint_redacted comes from ddcore.redact_url; never store the raw URL. client_version = web3_clientVersion when available (non-material); client_version_note appears when it was unavailable (drop it for the manifest).

identity._comment: status: MATCH when requested.chain_id == observed.chain_id (continue). OBSERVED_ONLY when no --chain-id was given and the observed chain was adopted: confirm the intended chain with the user, re-run with --chain-id N, and require MATCH before Step 2; never freeze in this state. CHAIN_MISMATCH means stop and report (rpc_probe exits 3 and reads nothing else); it is recorded HERE as an identity failure, never as a coverage limitation. UNVERIFIED means the chain id could not be read (exit 1; coverage limitation; nothing can be pinned). requested/observed repeat the two chain ids for the record. pin_warning appears when the block hash looks like a placeholder.

cache._comment: Binding of the --cache file to the live chain id: status none (no --cache), used, or ignored (the file was recorded for another chain and nothing was read from or written to it; note carries the reason). ddcore.ResponseCache keys entries on [chain_id, scheme, host, port, redacted path, method, params]; floating block tags are never cached; the chain id itself is always read live.

pin._comment: Primary pin P1 in manifest pin format. block_number, block_hash and timestamp_unix are copied from captured_header, the raw eth_getBlockByNumber result. Pin with --block finalized where the endpoint supports the tag, else latest, and say which in purpose. Every later read - and every later rpc_probe.py run against another contract - uses pinned_block_hex / --block <block_number>, never 'latest'. Additional chains and historical snapshots get P2..Pn in the manifest, never a replaced P1.

_comment_pinned_block_hex: Hex block number (0x..) passed to every pinned read.

runtime._comment: Target runtime at P1. code_hash = keccak256(eth_getCode) (0x + 64 hex). runtime_status: contract | eoa (no code at the pin: the empty-code hash, is_contract false; metadata and probes are then qualified) | unknown (eth_getCode failed or returned a non-string: a limitation is recorded and coverage_status is partial - never 'not a contract'). proxy.status: not_proxy | eip1967 | eip1822 | beacon | minimal_1167 | custom | unknown (unknown whenever a slot read failed, with a limitation; never not_proxy in that case). slots_read maps slot -> raw 32-byte value. upgrade_authority stays null until resolved under A-UPGRADE (address + role + threshold/timelock). Manifest: runtime_status goes to scope_addresses[0].runtime_status; is_contract and implementation_code_size are dropped.

metadata._comment: Resolved from the target with eth_call at P1. status: resolved | nonstandard (value kept, decoding basis in reason) | unresolved (value null, reason required; an empty string or control characters are unresolved). source names the call and pin; selector and raw preserve the request and raw return data (move raw into an evidence row and cite it via evidence_id when building the manifest). qualifier is null for a contract; for an eoa target every field is unresolved with the qualifier 'no runtime code at this address at the pin; return data cannot come from this address' (goes into reason in the manifest). accounting_model is yours to fill from code and behavior: standard_erc20 | rebasing | fee_on_transfer | shares_based | wrapper | unknown.

_comment_probes: Standard probes owner(), getOwner(), paused() plus each --call (a --call repeating a standard probe is read once). Element shape in _element_shapes.probe. status: ok | reverted | unavailable | empty. A revert is a fact about the contract at P1, not a limitation (recorded in failed_calls with outcome reverted); unavailable means the read failed and a limitation was recorded. For an eoa target every probe carries the qualifier and an ok/reverted result is marked INCONSISTENT in detail.

deployment._comment: Not derivable from standard JSON-RPC reads. Discover via explorer/trace tooling, then verify by receipt (contractAddress == target) and record provenance; until then status stays unresolved with the reason. deterministic = true when created via CREATE2/factory with a derivable address.
deployment.reason: deployment transaction is not derivable from standard JSON-RPC reads; discover it via explorer/trace tooling, then verify by receipt (contractAddress) and record provenance

_comment_candidate_pools: Pools from the architecture pass, each by exact address (v2/v3) or full pool key + derived PoolId (v4). Element shape in _element_shapes.candidate_pool. Canonical vs side is decided under B-CANON/B-SIDE, not here.
_comment_related_contracts: Every contract or key that can change balances, restrict transfers, remove principal, upgrade behavior (token AND reward/vault/distributor layer: G-LAYER-ADMIN), collect fees, allocate rewards, or enforce claimed utility; in focused mode only the asked question's dependencies (record the rest as an out_of_scope known limitation). Element shape = manifest scope_addresses entry (see _element_shapes.related_contract) so it can be copied unchanged after the target's own entry. Every address that will be named in the report needs an entry with a neutral role.
_comment_requirement_frame: The standard the verdict is judged against, e.g. 'rug resistance for a 30-day hold' or 'exit of 0.5% of supply within 5% degradation'. When the user gave none: 'rug resistance and exit at the stated size over a 30-day hold', labeled an assumption in the verdict.
_comment_scope_statement: What is in and out of scope (chains, pools, reward layers, time bounds).
materiality_rules: Monetary thresholds never apply to discovery of mint, upgrade, seizure, transfer-restriction, arbitrary-call, or LP-removal authority.
_comment_known_limitations: Free-text limitations known before starting (no archive endpoint, no explorer API, no parallel agents, focused run: authority surfaces not enumerated).
_comment_coverage_status: complete when limitations is empty, otherwise partial.
_comment_limitations: Manifest-shaped coverage limitations L1..Ln (see _element_shapes.limitation). Never token findings; a chain mismatch is never recorded here (it lives under identity).
_comment_calls: Every successful RPC call {method, params, cached} for replay.
_comment_failed_calls: Every failed call {method, params, cached, outcome (reverted|limitation), error_kind, error_message, limitation_id}.

_freeze._comment: Filled when the packet is frozen. sha256 = sha256 of this packet's JSON serialized with sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':') after setting EVERY value in this _freeze object to null (one-liner in references/target-packet.md and SKILL.md Step 1); frozen_at_utc; frozen_by (agent/session label, no personal data). Lanes verify by recomputing. After freezing, the packet is read-only; a new target or pin means a new packet.

candidate_pool.provenance: event_derived | rpc_derived | explorer_label | website_claim | inferred | user_supplied
candidate_pool.provenance_detail: e.g. PoolCreated log tx 0x.. block N; verify factory and init code hash at use time

related_contract.role: token | implementation | proxy_admin | beacon | owner | role_holder | multisig | timelock | pool | pool_manager | position_manager | position_nft | locker | hook | router | quoter | factory | launch_platform | curve | treasury | fee_recipient | vault | reward_distributor | bridge | oracle | deployer | launch_signer | funder | holder | burn | exchange_deposit | other
related_contract.provenance: user_supplied | rpc_derived | event_derived | explorer_label | website_claim | inferred

limitation.kind: rpc_timeout | rpc_rate_limit | rpc_pruned | rpc_error | dns_failure | api_unavailable | explorer_unavailable | source_unavailable | out_of_scope | other
